## Violations Fixed In-Phase

For each FIX-APPLIED entry: object name, line excerpt, what was changed, why.

## Questions

| # | Object:line | Question | Answer | Effect |
|---|-------------|----------|--------|--------|
| Q1 | {PROG}F01:120 | Should one failed item stop the whole run? | Intended — keep / Not intended — fix / Open / Auto: keep / Auto: fix (why) | none / FIX-APPLIED / open (if_not fix shown) |

## Final Verdict

✅ ALL PASS — proceed to Phase 8
or

```

Before anything is asked or decided, main drops every question that `decisions.md` (incl. the Phase 4 live consultant review lines — Phase 3.5 Step 1b) or `plan.md` § *Conflict Resolutions* already answers (`review-questions.md` § 1).

| `manual` / `hybrid` | Ask with `AskUserQuestion` (≤ 4 per call, `best` option first as *Recommended*). In `hybrid` this is the only stop between Phase 4 and Phase 8. |
| `auto` | Never ask. Apply `best` per `review-questions.md` § 6 and record it as auto-decided. |
| any mode, unattended per `review-questions.md` § 4 | Same as `auto`. |

- *Not intended — fix* or auto `fix` → one `FIX` line with `sev_if_not` and `if_not`; it joins the fix loop below like any finding. *Intended — keep* or auto `keep` → no fix. An auto `fix` that fails or does not converge is reverted and left open — never `❌ BLOCKED` (`review-questions.md` § 6).

They are listed in `review.md` § Questions, in the Phase 8 report (*Decisions & Assumptions* → *Open questions*, with the `if_not` fix) and in `handoff.md` open items. A later answer runs as `--fix` ([`cost-rules.md`](cost-rules.md) § 1c).

1	# Phase 6 — Bucket Parallelization + Model Escalation
2	
3	Authoritative rule for how `sap-code-reviewer` runs Phase 6 reviews in parallel buckets with a Sonnet→Opus escalation ladder. Referenced from `phase6-review.md`. This is the **default** strategy (`~/.sc4sap/preferences.json` → `phase6Strategy` = `buckets`); the opt-in alternative is [`phase6-detect-judge.md`](./phase6-detect-judge.md).
4	
5	**Read-only reviewer**: `sap-code-reviewer` has `disallowedTools: [Write, Edit]` and no `Update*` MCP tools. It **returns** bucket verdicts and fix lists as text; the main thread writes every file below and dispatches `sap-executor` for fixes.
6	
7	## Goal
8	
9	Cut Phase 6 wall-clock time by ~50% and Opus token cost by ~70% without losing review depth. Achieved by splitting the 12-item checklist into 4 independent buckets run on Sonnet in parallel, escalating to Opus only when MAJOR findings appear.
10	
11	## Bucket Definition
12	
13	The 12 convention items in `phase6-review.md` are split into 4 buckets. Each bucket is reviewed by a separate `Agent({subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-code-reviewer", model: "sonnet", ...})` dispatched in parallel.
14	
15	| Bucket | Items (from phase6-review.md) | Scope |
16	|--------|-------------------------------|-------|
17	| **B1 — ALV + UI** | #1 alv-rules, #2 text-element-rule | ALV field catalog, Docking vs Custom Control, text-Txx, MESSAGE literals; for ALV roles mapped to a code template, the template's DDIC / metadata-based field catalog method and container type are compliant (`alv-rules.md` § Code template exception) |
18	| **B2 — Logic Hygiene** | #3 constant-rule, #8 clean-code (shared baseline + paradigm-specific file) + business questions | Magic literals, SY-SUBRC, SELECT *, inline decl, commented code. B2 reviewer reads `interview.md` Paradigm dimension first, then loads `clean-code.md` + either `clean-code-oop.md` OR `clean-code-procedural.md` accordingly — never both. **B2 alone owns `QUESTION` detection** ([`../../common/review-questions.md`](../../common/review-questions.md) § 1): it also gets `spec.md`, `interview.md`, `consult-{module}.md`, `decisions.md` and `plan.md` (§ *Conflict Resolutions*) and reads the business logic (commits, status filters, amounts, org filters, error policy) against them. |
19	| **B3 — Structure + Naming** | #4 procedural-form-naming, #5 oop-pattern, #6 include-structure, #7 naming-conventions | Include suffix, class split, Z prefix, `_{screen_no}` FORM; for roles mapped to a code template, structure is checked against `templates/<NAME>/` instead ([`code-template.md`](code-template.md)) |
20	| **B4 — Platform + Config** | #9 abap-release-reference, #10 sap-version-reference, #11 spro-lookup, #12 activation-state | Release-allowed syntax, ECC vs S/4, SPRO tables, inactive objects |
21	
22	## Parallel Dispatch
23	
24	Parallel (single message, 4 tool-use blocks). Each call uses full JSON form:
25	
26	```
27	Agent({
28	  subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-code-reviewer",
29	  model: "sonnet",
30	  description: "Phase 6 review — bucket B1 (ALV + UI)",
31	  prompt: "Review bucket B1 covering items [1,2] (alv-rules, text-element-rule). See phase6-review.md for item specs and phase6-buckets.md for bucket scope."
32	})
33	Agent({
34	  subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-code-reviewer",
35	  model: "sonnet",
36	  description: "Phase 6 review — bucket B2 (Logic Hygiene)",
37	  prompt: "Review bucket B2 covering items [3,8] (constant-rule, clean-code) and the business questions. Read interview.md Paradigm dimension first; then load clean-code.md + one of clean-code-oop.md / clean-code-procedural.md accordingly. For QUESTION lines follow common/review-questions.md § 1–2 and § 6 (set best / why); inputs: <paths of spec.md, interview.md, consult-{module}.md, decisions.md, plan.md>."
38	})
39	Agent({
40	  subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-code-reviewer",
41	  model: "sonnet",
42	  description: "Phase 6 review — bucket B3 (Structure + Naming)",
43	  prompt: "Review bucket B3 covering items [4,5,6,7] (procedural-form-naming, oop-pattern, include-structure, naming-conventions)."
44	})
45	Agent({
46	  subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-code-reviewer",
47	  model: "sonnet",
48	  description: "Phase 6 review — bucket B4 (Platform + Config)",
49	  prompt: "Review bucket B4 covering items [9,10,11,12] (abap-release-reference, sap-version-reference, spro-lookup, activation-state)."
50	})
51	```
52	
53	Every bucket prompt ends with: "Return the verdict table as text plus one `FIX …` line per finding; do not write files." B2's prompt adds: "and one `QUESTION …` line per business-intent item." B1 / B3 / B4 never return `QUESTION` lines — a business doubt there is noted in one line for B2's scope, not fixed. Each bucket agent:
54	1. Fetches source of all created objects via MCP (`GetInclude`, `GetProgram`, etc.)
55	2. Runs its subset of checklist items
56	3. Classifies each finding `PASS` / `MINOR` / `MAJOR`, with one `FIX obj=<name> item=<§n> severity=<…> line=<n> change="<…>"` line per finding
57	4. Returns the verdict text — main writes it to `.sc4sap/program/{PROG}/review-bucket-{B1|B2|B3|B4}.md`
58	
59	Wait for all 4 buckets. Merge into consolidated `review.md`.
60	
61	## Finding Classification
62	
63	- **PASS** — no violation found
64	- **MINOR** — violation exists but non-blocking (e.g., a TEXT-Txx missing an optional tooltip). Main applies the `FIX` lines per [`cost-rules.md`](cost-rules.md) § 1a (main-thread Edit, or a fresh executor); once applied the item is recorded `FIX-APPLIED`.
65	- **MAJOR** — violation blocks Phase 8 (e.g., manual LVC_T_FCAT build, Docking replaced by Custom Control, ECC-deprecated pattern on S/4). Escalate per below.
66	- **QUESTION** — valid code whose correctness depends on business intent the inputs do not settle ([`../../common/review-questions.md`](../../common/review-questions.md)). Not counted below, not fixed; handled per [`phase6-output-format.md`](./phase6-output-format.md) § Business Questions after the merge (step 5 of § Merge Algorithm). Cap 5.
67	
68	## Model Escalation (6-3)
69	
70	After all 4 buckets finish, count MAJOR findings:
71	
72	| MAJOR count | Action |
73	|-------------|--------|
74	| **0** | Skip Opus. Merge bucket outputs into `review.md` → business questions (§ Merge Algorithm step 5) → apply MINOR and answer-driven fixes per [`cost-rules.md`](cost-rules.md) § 1a → final verdict `✅ ALL PASS` → Phase 8. |
75	| **1–2** | Dispatch `Agent({subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-code-reviewer", model: "opus", ...})` **scoped only to the MAJOR findings** — pass finding list + affected object names. Opus re-reviews and returns a confirmed fix list; main applies it per [`cost-rules.md`](cost-rules.md) § 1a, then re-runs a fresh Opus review on the diff of those findings only (up to 3 iterations per finding; never resume the earlier reviewer). Main writes the final verdict to `review.md`. |
76	| **3+** | Dispatch Opus with full context (all 4 bucket reports + source). Opus decides whether to fix (fix list → `sap-executor` as above) or BLOCK. If BLOCK, write `review.md` with `❌ BLOCKED` and surface to user. |
77	
78	Rationale: Sonnet is accurate enough to *detect* convention violations; Opus is reserved for *synthesizing fixes across multiple related findings* where reasoning depth matters.
79	
80	## Merge Algorithm
81	
82	After buckets (and optional Opus pass) complete:
83	
84	1. Read all 4 `review-bucket-{B*}.md` files
85	2. If Opus escalation ran, read its output too
86	3. Build consolidated `review.md` using the template in `phase6-review.md`, but with an added header:
87	   ```markdown
88	   **Review Strategy**: buckets — 4-bucket parallel (Sonnet) + {Opus escalation: yes/no, N findings}
89	   **Buckets**: B1 ALV+UI, B2 Logic, B3 Structure, B4 Platform
90	   **Timing**: parallel_sec={T1}, opus_sec={T2}, total_sec={T1+T2}
91	   ```
92	4. Delete the per-bucket files (they remain in git history if versioned; otherwise clean up to avoid clutter)
93	5. **Business questions** — B2's `QUESTION` lines (after any Opus pass) are asked or auto-decided per [`phase6-output-format.md`](./phase6-output-format.md) § Business Questions, before any fix is applied. A `FIX` that comes from an answer follows the path of its `sev_if_not`: MINOR → § 1a fix + diff re-review; MAJOR → the 1–2 MAJOR row above, scoped to that finding.

96	
97	- If any bucket agent crashes or times out: retry that bucket ONCE with the same model. On second failure, escalate to Opus immediately for that bucket's scope.
98	- If bucket verdicts conflict (e.g., B2 says constant-rule PASS, B3 says naming-conventions MAJOR on the same constant name): treat as MAJOR and include in Opus escalation.
99	- If user is in `manual` execution mode: after bucket parallel run, prompt before dispatching Opus escalation — user may choose to review MAJOR findings themselves instead. `hybrid` escalates like `auto`; its only stop is the business questions.
100

102

104	"6_review": {
105	  "status": "completed | blocked",
106	  "ts": "...",
107	  "strategy": "buckets",

116	}
117	```

120

# Phase 6 — Bucket Parallelization + Model Escalation

Authoritative rule for how `sap-code-reviewer` runs Phase 6 reviews in parallel buckets with a Sonnet→Opus escalation ladder. Referenced from `phase6-review.md`. This is the **default** strategy (`~/.sc4sap/preferences.json` → `phase6Strategy` = `buckets`); the opt-in alternative is [`phase6-detect-judge.md`](./phase6-detect-judge.md).

**Read-only reviewer**: `sap-code-reviewer` has `disallowedTools: [Write, Edit]` and no `Update*` MCP tools. It **returns** bucket verdicts and fix lists as text; the main thread writes every file below and dispatches `sap-executor` for fixes.

## Goal

Cut Phase 6 wall-clock time by ~50% and Opus token cost by ~70% without losing review depth. Achieved by splitting the 12-item checklist into 4 independent buckets run on Sonnet in parallel, escalating to Opus only when MAJOR findings appear.

## Bucket Definition

The 12 convention items in `phase6-review.md` are split into 4 buckets. Each bucket is reviewed by a separate `Agent({subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-code-reviewer", model: "sonnet", ...})` dispatched in parallel.

| Bucket | Items (from phase6-review.md) | Scope |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------|
| **B1 — ALV + UI** | #1 alv-rules, #2 text-element-rule | ALV field catalog, Docking vs Custom Control, text-Txx, MESSAGE literals; for ALV roles mapped to a code template, the template's DDIC / metadata-based field catalog method and container type are compliant (`alv-rules.md` § Code template exception) |
| **B2 — Logic Hygiene** | #3 constant-rule, #8 clean-code (shared baseline + paradigm-specific file) + business questions | Magic literals, SY-SUBRC, SELECT *, inline decl, commented code. B2 reviewer reads `interview.md` Paradigm dimension first, then loads `clean-code.md` + either `clean-code-oop.md` OR `clean-code-procedural.md` accordingly — never both. **B2 alone owns `QUESTION` detection** ([`../../common/review-questions.md`](../../common/review-questions.md) § 1): it also gets `spec.md`, `interview.md`, `consult-{module}.md`, `decisions.md` and `plan.md` (§ *Conflict Resolutions*) and reads the business logic (commits, status filters, amounts, org filters, error policy) against them. |
| **B3 — Structure + Naming** | #4 procedural-form-naming, #5 oop-pattern, #6 include-structure, #7 naming-conventions | Include suffix, class split, Z prefix, `_{screen_no}` FORM; for roles mapped to a code template, structure is checked against `templates/<NAME>/` instead ([`code-template.md`](code-template.md)) |
| **B4 — Platform + Config** | #9 abap-release-reference, #10 sap-version-reference, #11 spro-lookup, #12 activation-state | Release-allowed syntax, ECC vs S/4, SPRO tables, inactive objects |

## Parallel Dispatch

Parallel (single message, 4 tool-use blocks). Each call uses full JSON form:

```
Agent({
  subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-code-reviewer",
  model: "sonnet",
  description: "Phase 6 review — bucket B1 (ALV + UI)",
  prompt: "Review bucket B1 covering items [1,2] (alv-rules, text-element-rule). See phase6-review.md for item specs and phase6-buckets.md for bucket scope."
})
Agent({
  subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-code-reviewer",
  model: "sonnet",
  description: "Phase 6 review — bucket B2 (Logic Hygiene)",
  prompt: "Review bucket B2 covering items [3,8] (constant-rule, clean-code) and the business questions. Read interview.md Paradigm dimension first; then load clean-code.md + one of clean-code-oop.md / clean-code-procedural.md accordingly. For QUESTION lines follow common/review-questions.md § 1–2 and § 6 (set best / why); inputs: <paths of spec.md, interview.md, consult-{module}.md, decisions.md, plan.md>."
})
Agent({
  subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-code-reviewer",
  model: "sonnet",
  description: "Phase 6 review — bucket B3 (Structure + Naming)",
  prompt: "Review bucket B3 covering items [4,5,6,7] (procedural-form-naming, oop-pattern, include-structure, naming-conventions)."
})
Agent({
  subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-code-reviewer",
  model: "sonnet",
  description: "Phase 6 review — bucket B4 (Platform + Config)",
  prompt: "Review bucket B4 covering items [9,10,11,12] (abap-release-reference, sap-version-reference, spro-lookup, activation-state)."
})
```

Every bucket prompt ends with: "Return the verdict table as text plus one `FIX …` line per finding; do not write files." B2's prompt adds: "and one `QUESTION …` line per business-intent item." B1 / B3 / B4 never return `QUESTION` lines — a business doubt there is noted in one line for B2's scope, not fixed. Each bucket agent:
1. Fetches source of all created objects via MCP (`GetInclude`, `GetProgram`, etc.)
2. Runs its subset of checklist items
3. Classifies each finding `PASS` / `MINOR` / `MAJOR`, with one `FIX obj=<name> item=<§n> severity=<…> line=<n> change="<…>"` line per finding
4. Returns the verdict text — main writes it to `.sc4sap/program/{PROG}/review-bucket-{B1|B2|B3|B4}.md`

Wait for all 4 buckets. Merge into consolidated `review.md`.

## Finding Classification

- **PASS** — no violation found
- **MINOR** — violation exists but non-blocking (e.g., a TEXT-Txx missing an optional tooltip). Main applies the `FIX` lines per [`cost-rules.md`](cost-rules.md) § 1a (main-thread Edit, or a fresh executor); once applied the item is recorded `FIX-APPLIED`.
- **MAJOR** — violation blocks Phase 8 (e.g., manual LVC_T_FCAT build, Docking replaced by Custom Control, ECC-deprecated pattern on S/4). Escalate per below.
- **QUESTION** — valid code whose correctness depends on business intent the inputs do not settle ([`../../common/review-questions.md`](../../common/review-questions.md)). Not counted below, not fixed; handled per [`phase6-output-format.md`](./phase6-output-format.md) § Business Questions after the merge (step 5 of § Merge Algorithm). Cap 5.

## Model Escalation (6-3)

After all 4 buckets finish, count MAJOR findings:

| MAJOR count | Action |
|-------------|--------|
| **0** | Skip Opus. Merge bucket outputs into `review.md` → business questions (§ Merge Algorithm step 5) → apply MINOR and answer-driven fixes per [`cost-rules.md`](cost-rules.md) § 1a → final verdict `✅ ALL PASS` → Phase 8. |
| **1–2** | Dispatch `Agent({subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-code-reviewer", model: "opus", ...})` **scoped only to the MAJOR findings** — pass finding list + affected object names. Opus re-reviews and returns a confirmed fix list; main applies it per [`cost-rules.md`](cost-rules.md) § 1a, then re-runs a fresh Opus review on the diff of those findings only (up to 3 iterations per finding; never resume the earlier reviewer). Main writes the final verdict to `review.md`. |
| **3+** | Dispatch Opus with full context (all 4 bucket reports + source). Opus decides whether to fix (fix list → `sap-executor` as above) or BLOCK. If BLOCK, write `review.md` with `❌ BLOCKED` and surface to user. |

Rationale: Sonnet is accurate enough to *detect* convention violations; Opus is reserved for *synthesizing fixes across multiple related findings* where reasoning depth matters.

## Merge Algorithm

After buckets (and optional Opus pass) complete:

1. Read all 4 `review-bucket-{B*}.md` files
2. If Opus escalation ran, read its output too
3. Build consolidated `review.md` using the template in `phase6-review.md`, but with an added header:
   ```markdown
   **Review Strategy**: buckets — 4-bucket parallel (Sonnet) + {Opus escalation: yes/no, N findings}
   **Buckets**: B1 ALV+UI, B2 Logic, B3 Structure, B4 Platform
   **Timing**: parallel_sec={T1}, opus_sec={T2}, total_sec={T1+T2}
   ```
4. Delete the per-bucket files (they remain in git history if versioned; otherwise clean up to avoid clutter)
5. **Business questions** — B2's `QUESTION` lines (after any Opus pass) are asked or auto-decided per [`phase6-output-format.md`](./phase6-output-format.md) § Business Questions, before any fix is applied. A `FIX` that comes from an answer follows the path of its `sev_if_not`: MINOR → § 1a fix + diff re-review; MAJOR → the 1–2 MAJOR row above, scoped to that finding.

## Failure Handling

- If any bucket agent crashes or times out: retry that bucket ONCE with the same model. On second failure, escalate to Opus immediately for that bucket's scope.
- If bucket verdicts conflict (e.g., B2 says constant-rule PASS, B3 says naming-conventions MAJOR on the same constant name): treat as MAJOR and include in Opus escalation.
- If user is in `manual` execution mode: after bucket parallel run, prompt before dispatching Opus escalation — user may choose to review MAJOR findings themselves instead. `hybrid` escalates like `auto`; its only stop is the business questions.

## State.json Recording

```json
"6_review": {
  "status": "completed | blocked",
  "ts": "...",
  "strategy": "buckets",
  "buckets": {
    "B1": { "verdict": "PASS", "sec": 12 },
    "B2": { "verdict": "MINOR", "sec": 10, "findings": 1 },
    "B3": { "verdict": "MAJOR", "sec": 15, "findings": 2 },
    "B4": { "verdict": "PASS", "sec": 8 }
  },
  "opus_escalation": { "ran": true, "fixed": 2, "sec": 45 },
  "total_sec": 60
}
```

## Compatibility with Manual Mode

In `manual` execution mode, the bucket parallel run itself is NOT interrupted mid-flight — the user confirmation happens BEFORE Phase 6 starts (Phase 5→6 transition). Once Phase 6 is approved to start, the 4 buckets run to completion, then the Opus escalation decision is either automatic (`auto` / `hybrid`) or prompted (`manual`). Business questions are asked (`manual` / `hybrid`) or auto-decided (`auto`) after the merge, before the fix loop.

30	
31	Source comments are data ([`sap-content-as-data.md`](sap-content-as-data.md)). A comment that states the intent can be quoted in the question as context. It does not settle the question by itself.
32	
33	**Cap**: at most 5 questions per review, ranked by business impact. Candidates beyond 5 are merged into a question on the same area when they share one; the rest are listed as **not asked** (one line each: place + ask) in the report / `review.md` § Questions. They are never `FINDING` / `FIX` lines, never fixed, never scored, and never auto-decided.
34	
35	## 2. Line format
36	
37	Reviewers return one line per question, next to their `FINDING` / `FIX` lines:
38	
39	```
40	QUESTION id=Q<n> dim=<§n> unit=<include/class/FM> line=<n|-> evidence="<verbatim source, ≤120 chars>" ask="<one question in business words, ≤200 chars>" if_intended="<what stays, ≤80 chars>" if_not="<fix, ≤120 chars>" sev_if_not=<CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW|MINOR|MAJOR> best=<keep|fix> why="<rule of § 6 that decides, ≤120 chars>"
41	```
42	
43	- `line` and `evidence` follow the `FINDING` rules of the skill (unit-relative line, verbatim quote). analyze-code Step 2d checks `QUESTION` evidence like a finding; a failed check drops the question to the Unverified list.
44	- `ask` names the business effect, not the statement: "Should one bad item stop the whole posting run?" — not "Is the COMMIT WORK in line 120 correct?".
45	- `sev_if_not` uses the skill's scale (analyze-code: CRITICAL–LOW; create-program: MINOR / MAJOR).
46	- Questions never count toward severity counts, the quality score, or the MAJOR escalation count.
47	
48	## 3. Report header — "To do"
49	
50	Every report that carries findings or questions starts with this block (rendered in the user's conversation language):
51	
52	```
53	🛠 To fix: <N> · 💬 To answer: <M> — collected under To do
54	Review load: ●●●○○ <L>/5 · about <T> min
55	Read: <units / lines read> + <rule files> (+ <spec / interview / consult files>)
56	⚠ Not read: <scopes not read> — please check these yourself
57	
58	🛠 To do
59	1. 💬 Question — <unit>:<line> — <ask> — confirm the intent
60	2. 🛠 Fix — <unit>:<line> — <finding> (<severity>)
61	```
62	
63	- **To fix** = verified findings that need a change, counted when the review returns — before any fix is applied (analyze-code: all verified findings; create-program: MINOR + MAJOR). create-program then marks each line FIX-APPLIED as it is fixed.
64	- **Review load** — points: 3 per CRITICAL / MAJOR, 2 per HIGH, 2 per question, 1 per other finding. Level: 0–2 → 1, 3–5 → 2, 6–10 → 3, 11–20 → 4, > 20 → 5. **Minutes** ≈ 5 per CRITICAL / HIGH / MAJOR + 3 per question + 1 per other, rounded up to 5.
65	- **Not read** — list honestly what no agent looked at: unscanned or `BLOCKED` scopes, callers beyond the top 10, runtime data, customizing values, called standard code, other systems. Never leave it out; write `none` only when it is true.
66	- **To do** lists questions first, then fixes by severity. Long lists show the first 7 and the rest as `+<n> more`.
67	
68	## 4. Asking
69	
70	- Use `AskUserQuestion`, up to 4 questions per call (a second call for the 5th). Each question stands alone: object, `unit:line`, what the code does in plain words, and the business effect.
71	- Options per question: `Intended — keep` · `Not intended — fix` · `Not sure — leave open`. The option that matches `best` goes first with `(Recommended)` and its `why` in the description. The user's free text (Other) is read by main: clearly one of the first two → apply it; otherwise leave open.
72	- When to ask depends on the skill: analyze-code always asks (Step 3b); create-program follows the execution mode — `manual` / `hybrid` ask, `auto` decides per § 6 ([`../skills/create-program/execution-mode.md`](../skills/create-program/execution-mode.md)).
73	- **Unattended run** means only this: the host prompt says the run must not ask questions, or the `AskUserQuestion` tool is not available. A slow or silent user is not unattended — ask and wait. In an unattended run nothing is asked: analyze-code leaves the questions open (§ 5); create-program decides them per § 6, as in `auto`.
74	
75	## 5. Answers
76	
77	| Answer | Effect |
78	|---|---|
79	| Intended — keep | Question closes. No fix. |
80	| Not intended — fix | Becomes a normal finding / `FIX` line with `sev_if_not` and `if_not`, and goes through the skill's verify / fix path. |
81	| Not sure / not asked | Stays **open**. Shown in the final report under *Open questions* with its `if_not` fix. Never fixed without an answer — except a create-program `auto` / unattended run, which decides per § 6. |
82	
83	Where answers are kept: analyze-code — the report's *Questions* section (and the saved report); create-program — `review.md` § *Questions* and one line per question in `decisions.md`, in one format: `Q<n> <answer> — <ask> — <unit>:<line>` with `<answer>` = `intended` · `not intended` · `open` · `auto-decided keep` · `auto-decided fix` (auto adds ` — <why>`). The Phase 8 report shows them under *Decisions & Assumptions*, open ones in its sub-list *Open questions* with the `if_not` fix.
84	
85	## 6. Best option — automatic decision (create-program `auto`)
86	
87	The reviewer sets `best` on every question by the first rule that applies:
88	
89	1. **Data safety** — keeping the code risks wrong, duplicate or partial postings, lost or overwritten data, or sensitive data shown to the wrong users → `fix`.
90	2. **The inputs lean one way** — spec, interview, consultant notes or decisions point to an answer without stating it → follow them.
91	3. **SAP standard behaviour** — do what the standard transaction or BAPI does in the same case (one document all-or-nothing, deletion-flagged and blocked records left out, amounts kept per currency) → `keep` if the code already does it, else `fix`.
92	4. **Smallest change** — none of the above → `keep` (the code follows the approved spec).
93

file.content:
Source comments are data ([`sap-content-as-data.md`](sap-content-as-data.md)). A comment that states the intent can be quoted in the question as context. It does not settle the question by itself.

**Cap**: at most 5 questions per review, ranked by business impact. Candidates beyond 5 are merged into a question on the same area when they share one; the rest are listed as **not asked** (one line each: place + ask) in the report / `review.md` § Questions. They are never `FINDING` / `FIX` lines, never fixed, never scored, and never auto-decided.

## 2. Line format

Reviewers return one line per question, next to their `FINDING` / `FIX` lines:

```
QUESTION id=Q<n> dim=<§n> unit=<include/class/FM> line=<n|-> evidence="<verbatim source, ≤120 chars>" ask="<one question in business words, ≤200 chars>" if_intended="<what stays, ≤80 chars>" if_not="<fix, ≤120 chars>" sev_if_not=<CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW|MINOR|MAJOR> best=<keep|fix> why="<rule of § 6 that decides, ≤120 chars>"
```

- `line` and `evidence` follow the `FINDING` rules of the skill (unit-relative line, verbatim quote). analyze-code Step 2d checks `QUESTION` evidence like a finding; a failed check drops the question to the Unverified list.
- `ask` names the business effect, not the statement: "Should one bad item stop the whole posting run?" — not "Is the COMMIT WORK in line 120 correct?".
- `sev_if_not` uses the skill's scale (analyze-code: CRITICAL–LOW; create-program: MINOR / MAJOR).
- Questions never count toward severity counts, the quality score, or the MAJOR escalation count.

## 3. Report header — "To do"

Every report that carries findings or questions starts with this block (rendered in the user's conversation language):

```
🛠 To fix: <N> · 💬 To answer: <M> — collected under To do
Review load: ●●●○○ <L>/5 · about <T> min
Read: <units / lines read> + <rule files> (+ <spec / interview / consult files>)
⚠ Not read: <scopes not read> — please check these yourself

🛠 To do
1. 💬 Question — <unit>:<line> — <ask> — confirm the intent
2. 🛠 Fix — <unit>:<line> — <finding> (<severity>)
```

- **To fix** = verified findings that need a change, counted when the review returns — before any fix is applied (analyze-code: all verified findings; create-program: MINOR + MAJOR). create-program then marks each line FIX-APPLIED as it is fixed.
- **Review load** — points: 3 per CRITICAL / MAJOR, 2 per HIGH, 2 per question, 1 per other finding. Level: 0–2 → 1, 3–5 → 2, 6–10 → 3, 11–20 → 4, > 20 → 5. **Minutes** ≈ 5 per CRITICAL / HIGH / MAJOR + 3 per question + 1 per other, rounded up to 5.
- **Not read** — list honestly what no agent looked at: unscanned or `BLOCKED` scopes, callers beyond the top 10, runtime data, customizing values, called standard code, other systems. Never leave it out; write `none` only when it is true.
- **To do** lists questions first, then fixes by severity. Long lists show the first 7 and the rest as `+<n> more`.

## 4. Asking

- Use `AskUserQuestion`, up to 4 questions per call (a second call for the 5th). Each question stands alone: object, `unit:line`, what the code does in plain words, and the business effect.
- Options per question: `Intended — keep` · `Not intended — fix` · `Not sure — leave open`. The option that matches `best` goes first with `(Recommended)` and its `why` in the description. The user's free text (Other) is read by main: clearly one of the first two → apply it; otherwise leave open.
- When to ask depends on the skill: analyze-code always asks (Step 3b); create-program follows the execution mode — `manual` / `hybrid` ask, `auto` decides per § 6 ([`../skills/create-program/execution-mode.md`](../skills/create-program/execution-mode.md)).
- **Unattended run** means only this: the host prompt says the run must not ask questions, or the `AskUserQuestion` tool is not available. A slow or silent user is not unattended — ask and wait. In an unattended run nothing is asked: analyze-code leaves the questions open (§ 5); create-program decides them per § 6, as in `auto`.

## 5. Answers

| Answer | Effect |
|---|---|
| Intended — keep | Question closes. No fix. |
| Not intended — fix | Becomes a normal finding / `FIX` line with `sev_if_not` and `if_not`, and goes through the skill's verify / fix path. |
| Not sure / not asked | Stays **open**. Shown in the final report under *Open questions* with its `if_not` fix. Never fixed without an answer — except a create-program `auto` / unattended run, which decides per § 6. |

Where answers are kept: analyze-code — the report's *Questions* section (and the saved report); create-program — `review.md` § *Questions* and one line per question in `decisions.md`, in one format: `Q<n> <answer> — <ask> — <unit>:<line>` with `<answer>` = `intended` · `not intended` · `open` · `auto-decided keep` · `auto-decided fix` (auto adds ` — <why>`). The Phase 8 report shows them under *Decisions & Assumptions*, open ones in its sub-list *Open questions* with the `if_not` fix.

## 6. Best option — automatic decision (create-program `auto`)

The reviewer sets `best` on every question by the first rule that applies:

1. **Data safety** — keeping the code risks wrong, duplicate or partial postings, lost or overwritten data, or sensitive data shown to the wrong users → `fix`.
2. **The inputs lean one way** — spec, interview, consultant notes or decisions point to an answer without stating it → follow them.
3. **SAP standard behaviour** — do what the standard transaction or BAPI does in the same case (one document all-or-nothing, deletion-flagged and blocked records left out, amounts kept per currency) → `keep` if the code already does it, else `fix`.
4. **Smallest change** — none of the above → `keep` (the code follows the approved spec).

Main applies `best` without asking: `fix` → one `FIX` line from `if_not` / `sev_if_not`, through the normal fix loop and diff re-review; `keep` → no change. An auto `fix` must never block a valid program: if it fails activation or does not pass its re-review within the fix loop's iterations, revert it, append `Q<n> open — reverted auto fix — <ask> — <unit>:<line>` to `decisions.md` (the newest line per `Q<n>` wins; the question then shows under *Open questions*, not as decided), and go on — it never leads to `❌ BLOCKED`. Each decision is recorded as **auto-decided** in three places:
- `review.md` § *Questions* — answer `Auto: keep` / `Auto: fix` with `why`.
- `decisions.md` — per § 5 (`Q<n> auto-decided <keep|fix> — <ask> — <unit>:<line> — <why>`).
- Phase 8 report — section *Business questions decided automatically*, right after the Evidence block: per question the code place, the question, the decision, the reason and how to reverse it (`/sc4sap:create-program {PROG} --fix "reverse Q<n>"`). The report is then always also written as `report.html` (no y/N), so the decisions sit in the result HTML.

1	# Phase 6 — Review Output Format + Failure Handling
2	
3	Companion file split from [`phase6-review.md`](./phase6-review.md) to keep each MD under the 200-line limit. The convention checklist lives in `phase6-review.md`; this file is the authoritative source for the report artifact format and the violation-fix loop.
4	
5	## Output File Format
6	
7	Write to `.sc4sap/program/{PROG}/review.md`:
8	
9	```markdown
10	# Phase 6 Review — {PROG}
11	
12	**Date**: YYYY-MM-DD
13	**Reviewer Agent**: sap-code-reviewer
14	**Strategy**: buckets | detect-judge
15	**Spec ref**: spec.md
16	**Objects reviewed**: list of N objects
17	
18	<To do header — common/review-questions.md § 3: to fix / to answer, review load, read, not read, To do list>
19	
20	## Conventions Checked
21	
22	| # | Convention | Verdict | Notes |
23	|---|------------|---------|-------|
24	| 1 | alv-rules.md           | PASS / FIX-APPLIED / N/A | Screen flow logic, GUI PFKEYS verified |
25	| 2 | text-element-rule.md   | ... | counts.I / S / R / H verified |
26	| 3 | constant-rule.md       | ... | ... |
27	| 4 | procedural-form-naming | ... | ... |
28	| 5 | oop-pattern.md         | ... | ... |
29	| 6 | include-structure.md   | ... | Procedural-`E` absence verified |
30	| 7 | naming-conventions.md  | ... | ... |
31	| 8 | clean-code.md          | ... | ... |
32	| 9 | abap-release-reference | ... | ... |
33	| 10| sap-version-reference  | ... | ... |
34	| 11| spro-lookup.md         | ... | ... |
35	| 12| Activation state       | ... | GetInactiveObjects=0 for {PROG}* |
36	
37	## Violations Fixed In-Phase
38	
39	For each FIX-APPLIED entry: object name, line excerpt, what was changed, why.
40	
41	## Questions
42	
43	| # | Object:line | Question | Answer | Effect |
44	|---|-------------|----------|--------|--------|
45	| Q1 | {PROG}F01:120 | Should one failed item stop the whole run? | Intended — keep / Not intended — fix / Open / Auto: keep / Auto: fix (why) | none / FIX-APPLIED / open (if_not fix shown) |
46	
47	## Final Verdict
48	
49	✅ ALL PASS — proceed to Phase 8
50	or
51	❌ BLOCKED — list residual violations and reason
52	```
53	
54	## Business Questions
55	
56	Runs after the merge (buckets) or the judge (detect-judge) and BEFORE the first fix dispatch. Rules: [`../../common/review-questions.md`](../../common/review-questions.md).
57	
58	Before anything is asked or decided, main drops every question that `decisions.md` (incl. the Phase 4 live consultant review lines — Phase 3.5 Step 1b) or `plan.md` § *Conflict Resolutions* already answers (`review-questions.md` § 1).
59	
60	| Mode (`state.json` → `execution_mode`) | What happens |
61	|---|---|
62	| `manual` / `hybrid` | Ask with `AskUserQuestion` (≤ 4 per call, `best` option first as *Recommended*). In `hybrid` this is the only stop between Phase 4 and Phase 8. |
63	| `auto` | Never ask. Apply `best` per `review-questions.md` § 6 and record it as auto-decided. |
64	| any mode, unattended per `review-questions.md` § 4 | Same as `auto`. |
65	
66	- *Not intended — fix* or auto `fix` → one `FIX` line with `sev_if_not` and `if_not`; it joins the fix loop below like any finding. *Intended — keep* or auto `keep` → no fix. Each question is one line in `decisions.md` in the format of `review-questions.md` § 5. An auto `fix` that fails or does not converge is reverted and left open — never `❌ BLOCKED` (`review-questions.md` § 6).
67	- Open and not-asked questions never block the verdict — they are not convention violations, and the Phase 8 gate ignores `review.md` § Questions. They are listed in `review.md` § Questions, in the Phase 8 report (*Decisions & Assumptions* → *Open questions*, with the `if_not` fix) and in `handoff.md` open items. A later answer runs as `--fix` ([`cost-rules.md`](cost-rules.md) § 1c).
68	- Auto-decided questions go into the Phase 8 report section *Business questions decided automatically* and force the `report.html` copy (`review-questions.md` § 6).
69	
70	## Failure Handling
71	
72	- On any violation: the reviewer (read-only) returns a `FIX` line per finding and the fix is applied per [`cost-rules.md`](cost-rules.md) § 1a (small fix: main-thread Edit; larger: a fresh `sap-executor` with the `FIX` lines only; never a resumed agent) via `Update*` and re-activated. Documentation-only flagging is NOT acceptable — every confirmed finding is fixed or the run ends `❌ BLOCKED` (auto-decided fixes excepted: reverted and left open, `review-questions.md` § 6).
73	- After all fixes, re-verify the diff only (changed lines + enclosing FORM / method, scoped to the fixed findings); skip it when every fixed finding was MINOR (none touched a MAJOR-class item) and syntax check + activation + inactive check pass. Loop until ALL PASS or 3 iterations exhausted.
74	- If 3 iterations exhausted with residual violations: STOP, write `review.md` with `❌ BLOCKED`, surface to user with the specific violation list. Phase 8 is blocked.
75	
76	## False-Positive Patterns That Reviewer MUST Reject
77	
78	These patterns have been observed as "PASS" reports that later turned out to be broken. Reviewer must actively detect them — absence of evidence is a fail, not a pass.
79	
80	- **Screen created but flow logic commented out** — `flow_logic` contains only `* MODULE STATUS_xxxx.` / `* MODULE USER_COMMAND_xxxx.` (leading `*`). Empty runtime behavior.
81	- **GUI Status created but empty** — `definition.STA[*].CODE` exists yet no PFKEYS array and no application toolbar codes. Toolbar renders blank.
82	- **Text pool partial** — `counts.I > 0` but `counts.S == 0` while source declares `SELECT-OPTIONS` / `PARAMETERS`. Selection screen shows technical names.
83	- **Include created but not activated** — `GetInactiveObjects` shows `{PROG}{SUFFIX}` entries after the main program was reported as activated. Main program runs but throws `LOAD_PROGRAM_LOST` at a PERFORM call.
84	- **Procedural paradigm with an `{PROG}E` include** — event blocks relocated out of Main body; forbidden per `common/include-structure.md`.
85	- **Main program with no `INCLUDE` statements while plan says N includes exist** — executor inlined every declaration into Main; violates `main-program.abap` template and the include-structure convention.
86	- **OK_CODE binding broken** — any of: (a) screen has an OKCODE field with no `NAME` or a `NAME` that is not the TOP OK_CODE variable, (b) TOP include declares no OK_CODE variable (`OK_CODE`, `GV_OKCODE`, …) despite a screen being present, or (c) PAI (module, user-command FORM or method) does `CASE sy-ucomm.`. A missing local copy + `CLEAR` is only MINOR. Runs on the main screen; fails silently on the first popup or ALV toolbar event. See `common/ok-code-pattern.md`.
87

1	# Phase 6 — Bucket Parallelization + Model Escalation
2	
3	Authoritative rule for how `sap-code-reviewer` runs Phase 6 reviews in parallel buckets with a Sonnet→Opus escalation ladder. Referenced from `phase6-review.md`. This is the **default** strategy (`~/.sc4sap/preferences.json` → `phase6Strategy` = `buckets`); the opt-in alternative is [`phase6-detect-judge.md`](./phase6-detect-judge.md).
4	
5	**Read-only reviewer**: `sap-code-reviewer` has `disallowedTools: [Write, Edit]` and no `Update*` MCP tools. It **returns** bucket verdicts and fix lists as text; the main thread writes every file below and dispatches `sap-executor` for fixes.
6	
7	## Goal
8	
9	Cut Phase 6 wall-clock time by ~50% and Opus token cost by ~70% without losing review depth. Achieved by splitting the 12-item checklist into 4 independent buckets run on Sonnet in parallel, escalating to Opus only when MAJOR findings appear.
10	
11	## Bucket Definition
12	
13	The 12 convention items in `phase6-review.md` are split into 4 buckets. Each bucket is reviewed by a separate `Agent({subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-code-reviewer", model: "sonnet", ...})` dispatched in parallel.
14	
15	| Bucket | Items (from phase6-review.md) | Scope |
16	|--------|-------------------------------|-------|
17	| **B1 — ALV + UI** | #1 alv-rules, #2 text-element-rule | ALV field catalog, Docking vs Custom Control, text-Txx, MESSAGE literals; for ALV roles mapped to a code template, the template's DDIC / metadata-based field catalog method and container type are compliant (`alv-rules.md` § Code template exception) |
18	| **B2 — Logic Hygiene** | #3 constant-rule, #8 clean-code (shared baseline + paradigm-specific file) + business questions | Magic literals, SY-SUBRC, SELECT *, inline decl, commented code. B2 reviewer reads `interview.md` Paradigm dimension first, then loads `clean-code.md` + either `clean-code-oop.md` OR `clean-code-procedural.md` accordingly — never both. **B2 alone owns `QUESTION` detection** ([`../../common/review-questions.md`](../../common/review-questions.md) § 1): it also gets `spec.md`, `interview.md`, `consult-{module}.md`, `decisions.md` and `plan.md` (§ *Conflict Resolutions*) and reads the business logic (commits, status filters, amounts, org filters, error policy) against them. |
19	| **B3 — Structure + Naming** | #4 procedural-form-naming, #5 oop-pattern, #6 include-structure, #7 naming-conventions | Include suffix, class split, Z prefix, `_{screen_no}` FORM; for roles mapped to a code template, structure is checked against `templates/<NAME>/` instead ([`code-template.md`](code-template.md)) |
20	| **B4 — Platform + Config** | #9 abap-release-reference, #10 sap-version-reference, #11 spro-lookup, #12 activation-state | Release-allowed syntax, ECC vs S/4, SPRO tables, inactive objects |
21	
22	## Parallel Dispatch
23	
24	Parallel (single message, 4 tool-use blocks). Each call uses full JSON form:
25	
26	```
27	Agent({
28	  subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-code-reviewer",
29	  model: "sonnet",
30	  description: "Phase 6 review — bucket B1 (ALV + UI)",
31	  prompt: "Review bucket B1 covering items [1,2] (alv-rules, text-element-rule). See phase6-review.md for item specs and phase6-buckets.md for bucket scope."
32	})
33	Agent({
34	  subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-code-reviewer",
35	  model: "sonnet",
36	  description: "Phase 6 review — bucket B2 (Logic Hygiene)",
37	  prompt: "Review bucket B2 covering items [3,8] (constant-rule, clean-code) and the business questions. Read interview.md Paradigm dimension first; then load clean-code.md + one of clean-code-oop.md / clean-code-procedural.md accordingly. For QUESTION lines follow common/review-questions.md § 1–2 and § 6 (set best / why); inputs: <paths of spec.md, interview.md, consult-{module}.md, decisions.md, plan.md>."
38	})
39	Agent({
40	  subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-code-reviewer",
41	  model: "sonnet",
42	  description: "Phase 6 review — bucket B3 (Structure + Naming)",
43	  prompt: "Review bucket B3 covering items [4,5,6,7] (procedural-form-naming, oop-pattern, include-structure, naming-conventions)."
44	})
45	Agent({
46	  subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-code-reviewer",
47	  model: "sonnet",
48	  description: "Phase 6 review — bucket B4 (Platform + Config)",
49	  prompt: "Review bucket B4 covering items [9,10,11,12] (abap-release-reference, sap-version-reference, spro-lookup, activation-state)."
50	})
51	```
52	
53	Every bucket prompt ends with: "Return the verdict table as text plus one `FIX …` line per finding; do not write files." B2's prompt adds: "and one `QUESTION …` line per business-intent item." B1 / B3 / B4 never return `QUESTION` lines — a business doubt there is noted in one line for B2's scope, not fixed. Each bucket agent:
54	1. Fetches source of all created objects via MCP (`GetInclude`, `GetProgram`, etc.)
55	2. Runs its subset of checklist items
56	3. Classifies each finding `PASS` / `MINOR` / `MAJOR`, with one `FIX obj=<name> item=<§n> severity=<…> line=<n> change="<…>"` line per finding
57	4. Returns the verdict text — main writes it to `.sc4sap/program/{PROG}/review-bucket-{B1|B2|B3|B4}.md`
58	
59	Wait for all 4 buckets. Merge into consolidated `review.md`.
60	
61	## Finding Classification
62	
63	- **PASS** — no violation found
64	- **MINOR** — violation exists but non-blocking (e.g., a TEXT-Txx missing an optional tooltip). Main applies the `FIX` lines per [`cost-rules.md`](cost-rules.md) § 1a (main-thread Edit, or a fresh executor); once applied the item is recorded `FIX-APPLIED`.
65	- **MAJOR** — violation blocks Phase 8 (e.g., manual LVC_T_FCAT build, Docking replaced by Custom Control, ECC-deprecated pattern on S/4). Escalate per below.
66	- **QUESTION** — valid code whose correctness depends on business intent the inputs do not settle ([`../../common/review-questions.md`](../../common/review-questions.md)). Not counted below, not fixed; handled per [`phase6-output-format.md`](./phase6-output-format.md) § Business Questions after the merge (step 5 of § Merge Algorithm). Cap 5.
67	
68	## Model Escalation (6-3)
69	
70	After all 4 buckets finish, count MAJOR findings:
71	
72	| MAJOR count | Action |
73	|-------------|--------|
74	| **0** | Skip Opus. Merge bucket outputs into `review.md` → business questions (§ Merge Algorithm step 5) → apply MINOR and answer-driven fixes per [`cost-rules.md`](cost-rules.md) § 1a → final verdict `✅ ALL PASS` → Phase 8. |
75	| **1–2** | Dispatch `Agent({subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-code-reviewer", model: "opus", ...})` **scoped only to the MAJOR findings** — pass finding list + affected object names. Opus re-reviews and returns a confirmed fix list; main applies it per [`cost-rules.md`](cost-rules.md) § 1a, then re-runs a fresh Opus review on the diff of those findings only (up to 3 iterations per finding; never resume the earlier reviewer). Main writes the final verdict to `review.md`. |
76	| **3+** | Dispatch Opus with full context (all 4 bucket reports + source). Opus decides whether to fix (fix list → `sap-executor` as above) or BLOCK. If BLOCK, write `review.md` with `❌ BLOCKED` and surface to user. |
77	
78	Rationale: Sonnet is accurate enough to *detect* convention violations; Opus is reserved for *synthesizing fixes across multiple related findings* where reasoning depth matters.
79	
80	## Merge Algorithm
81	
82	After buckets (and optional Opus pass) complete:
83	
84	1. Read all 4 `review-bucket-{B*}.md` files
85	2. If Opus escalation ran, read its output too
86	3. Build consolidated `review.md` using the template in `phase6-review.md`, but with an added header:
87	   ```markdown
88	   **Review Strategy**: buckets — 4-bucket parallel (Sonnet) + {Opus escalation: yes/no, N findings}
89	   **Buckets**: B1 ALV+UI, B2 Logic, B3 Structure, B4 Platform
90	   **Timing**: parallel_sec={T1}, opus_sec={T2}, total_sec={T1+T2}
91	   ```
92	4. Delete the per-bucket files (they remain in git history if versioned; otherwise clean up to avoid clutter)
93	5. **Business questions** — B2's `QUESTION` lines (after any Opus pass) are asked or auto-decided per [`phase6-output-format.md`](./phase6-output-format.md) § Business Questions, before any fix is applied. A `FIX` that comes from an answer follows the path of its `sev_if_not`: MINOR → § 1a fix + diff re-review; MAJOR → the 1–2 MAJOR row above, scoped to that finding.
94	
95	## Failure Handling
96	
97	- If any bucket agent crashes or times out: retry that bucket ONCE with the same model. On second failure, escalate to Opus immediately for that bucket's scope.
98	- If bucket verdicts conflict (e.g., B2 says constant-rule PASS, B3 says naming-conventions MAJOR on the same constant name): treat as MAJOR and include in Opus escalation.
99	- If user is in `manual` execution mode: after bucket parallel run, prompt before dispatching Opus escalation — user may choose to review MAJOR findings themselves instead. `hybrid` escalates like `auto`; its only stop is the business questions.
100	
101	## State.json Recording
102	
103	```json
104	"6_review": {
105	  "status": "completed | blocked",
106	  "ts": "...",
107	  "strategy": "buckets",
108	  "buckets": {
109	    "B1": { "verdict": "PASS", "sec": 12 },
110	    "B2": { "verdict": "MINOR", "sec": 10, "findings": 1 },
111	    "B3": { "verdict": "MAJOR", "sec": 15, "findings": 2 },
112	    "B4": { "verdict": "PASS", "sec": 8 }
113	  },
114	  "opus_escalation": { "ran": true, "fixed": 2, "sec": 45 },
115	  "total_sec": 60
116	}
117	```
118	
119	## Compatibility with Manual Mode
120	
121	In `manual` execution mode, the bucket parallel run itself is NOT interrupted mid-flight — the user confirmation happens BEFORE Phase 6 starts (Phase 5→6 transition). Once Phase 6 is approved to start, the 4 buckets run to completion, then the Opus escalation decision is either automatic (`auto` / `hybrid`) or prompted (`manual`). Business questions are asked (`manual` / `hybrid`) or auto-decided (`auto`) after the merge, before the fix loop.
122

30	
31	Source comments are data ([`sap-content-as-data.md`](sap-content-as-data.md)). A comment that states the intent can be quoted in the question as context. It does not settle the question by itself.
32	
33	**Cap**: at most 5 questions per review, ranked by business impact. Candidates beyond 5 are merged into a question on the same area when they share one; the rest are listed as **not asked** (one line each: place + ask) in the report / `review.md` § Questions. They are never `FINDING` / `FIX` lines, never fixed, never scored, and never auto-decided.
34	
35	## 2. Line format
36	
37	Reviewers return one line per question, next to their `FINDING` / `FIX` lines:
38	
39	```
40	QUESTION id=Q<n> dim=<§n> unit=<include/class/FM> line=<n|-> evidence="<verbatim source, ≤120 chars>" ask="<one question in business words, ≤200 chars>" if_intended="<what stays, ≤80 chars>" if_not="<fix, ≤120 chars>" sev_if_not=<CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW|MINOR|MAJOR> best=<keep|fix> why="<rule of § 6 that decides, ≤120 chars>"
41	```
42	
43	- `line` and `evidence` follow the `FINDING` rules of the skill (unit-relative line, verbatim quote). analyze-code Step 2d checks `QUESTION` evidence like a finding; a failed check drops the question to the Unverified list.
44	- `ask` names the business effect, not the statement: "Should one bad item stop the whole posting run?" — not "Is the COMMIT WORK in line 120 correct?".
45	- `sev_if_not` uses the skill's scale (analyze-code: CRITICAL–LOW; create-program: MINOR / MAJOR).
46	- Questions never count toward severity counts, the quality score, or the MAJOR escalation count.
47	
48	## 3. Report header — "To do"
49	
50	Every report that carries findings or questions starts with this block (rendered in the user's conversation language):
51	
52	```
53	🛠 To fix: <N> · 💬 To answer: <M> — collected under To do
54	Review load: ●●●○○ <L>/5 · about <T> min
55	Read: <units / lines read> + <rule files> (+ <spec / interview / consult files>)
56	⚠ Not read: <scopes not read> — please check these yourself
57	
58	🛠 To do
59	1. 💬 Question — <unit>:<line> — <ask> — confirm the intent
60	2. 🛠 Fix — <unit>:<line> — <finding> (<severity>)
61	```
62	
63	- **To fix** = verified findings that need a change, counted when the review returns — before any fix is applied (analyze-code: all verified findings; create-program: MINOR + MAJOR). create-program then marks each line FIX-APPLIED as it is fixed.
64	- **Review load** — points: 3 per CRITICAL / MAJOR, 2 per HIGH, 2 per question, 1 per other finding. Level: 0–2 → 1, 3–5 → 2, 6–10 → 3, 11–20 → 4, > 20 → 5. **Minutes** ≈ 5 per CRITICAL / HIGH / MAJOR + 3 per question + 1 per other, rounded up to 5.
65	- **Not read** — list honestly what no agent looked at: unscanned or `BLOCKED` scopes, callers beyond the top 10, runtime data, customizing values, called standard code, other systems. Never leave it out; write `none` only when it is true.
66	- **To do** lists questions first, then fixes by severity. Long lists show the first 7 and the rest as `+<n> more`.
67	
68	## 4. Asking
69	
70	- Use `AskUserQuestion`, up to 4 questions per call (a second call for the 5th). Each question stands alone: object, `unit:line`, what the code does in plain words, and the business effect.
71	- Options per question: `Intended — keep` · `Not intended — fix` · `Not sure — leave open`. The option that matches `best` goes first with `(Recommended)` and its `why` in the description. The user's free text (Other) is read by main: clearly one of the first two → apply it; otherwise leave open.
72	- When to ask depends on the skill: analyze-code always asks (Step 3b); create-program follows the execution mode — `manual` / `hybrid` ask, `auto` decides per § 6 ([`../skills/create-program/execution-mode.md`](../skills/create-program/execution-mode.md)).
73	- **Unattended run** means only this: the host prompt says the run must not ask questions, or the `AskUserQuestion` tool is not available. A slow or silent user is not unattended — ask and wait. In an unattended run nothing is asked: analyze-code leaves the questions open (§ 5); create-program decides them per § 6, as in `auto`.
74	
75	## 5. Answers
76	
77	| Answer | Effect |
78	|---|---|
79	| Intended — keep | Question closes. No fix. |
80	| Not intended — fix | Becomes a normal finding / `FIX` line with `sev_if_not` and `if_not`, and goes through the skill's verify / fix path. |
81	| Not sure / not asked | Stays **open**. Shown in the final report under *Open questions* with its `if_not` fix. Never fixed without an answer — except a create-program `auto` / unattended run, which decides per § 6. |
82	
83	Where answers are kept: analyze-code — the report's *Questions* section (and the saved report); create-program — `review.md` § *Questions* and one line per question in `decisions.md`, in one format: `Q<n> <answer> — <ask> — <unit>:<line>` with `<answer>` = `intended` · `not intended` · `open` · `auto-decided keep` · `auto-decided fix` (auto adds ` — <why>`). The Phase 8 report shows them under *Decisions & Assumptions*, open ones in its sub-list *Open questions* with the `if_not` fix.
84	
85	## 6. Best option — automatic decision (create-program `auto`)
86	
87	The reviewer sets `best` on every question by the first rule that applies:
88	
89	1. **Data safety** — keeping the code risks wrong, duplicate or partial postings, lost or overwritten data, or sensitive data shown to the wrong users → `fix`.
90	2. **The inputs lean one way** — spec, interview, consultant notes or decisions point to an answer without stating it → follow them.
91	3. **SAP standard behaviour** — do what the standard transaction or BAPI does in the same case (one document all-or-nothing, deletion-flagged and blocked records left out, amounts kept per currency) → `keep` if the code already does it, else `fix`.
92	4. **Smallest change** — none of the above → `keep` (the code follows the approved spec).
93	
94	Main applies `best` without asking: `fix` → one `FIX` line from `if_not` / `sev_if_not`, through the normal fix loop and diff re-review; `keep` → no change. An auto `fix` must never block a valid program: if it fails activation or does not pass its re-review within the fix loop's iterations, revert it, append `Q<n> open — reverted auto fix — <ask> — <unit>:<line>` to `decisions.md` (the newest line per `Q<n>` wins; the question then shows under *Open questions*, not as decided), and go on — it never leads to `❌ BLOCKED`. Each decision is recorded as **auto-decided** in three places:
95	- `review.md` § *Questions* — answer `Auto: keep` / `Auto: fix` with `why`.
96	- `decisions.md` — per § 5 (`Q<n> auto-decided <keep|fix> — <ask> — <unit>:<line> — <why>`).
97	- Phase 8 report — section *Business questions decided automatically*, right after the Evidence block: per question the code place, the question, the decision, the reason and how to reverse it (`/sc4sap:create-program {PROG} --fix "reverse Q<n>"`). The report is then always also written as `report.html` (no y/N), so the decisions sit in the result HTML.

# Decisions — ZMMR_HQ_HYB

## Phase 4 Wave 3 (sap-executor, Sonnet·medium)
- STATUS_0100 FORM sets the GUI status and title, then PERFORMs INIT_ALV_0100. The screen flow needs only `MODULE status_0100` in PBO, as the spec says. No separate init module.
- Added `EKKO-BSTYP = 'F'` to the SELECT. BAPI_PO_CHANGE handles purchase orders only, not RFQs or contracts. The spec is silent on this.
- S_EKORG is required in code only: E01 is raised on F8 (sy-ucomm = ONLI) when S_EKORG is empty. This keeps the multiple-selection popups usable. Reason: the authority check (c) runs per purchasing organization, so an empty EKORG would bypass it.
- Authority check: reads T024E for the EKORGs in the selection, then AUTHORITY-CHECK M_BEST_EKO ACTVT 02 for each. M07 is raised as an error on the first miss. UNCONFIRMED (c).
- UNCONFIRMED (a) in DELIVERY_COMPLETED_0100. UNCONFIRMED (b) in READ_DATA: LOEKZ = space on EKKO and EKPO; blocked items stay visible and BLK_REASON_ID is shown. UNCONFIRMED (c) in CHECK_COMMON_AUTHORITY.
- EKBE is read with the full key (zekkn, vgabe, gjahr, belnr, buzei), because FOR ALL ENTRIES drops duplicate rows and would give a wrong net GR.
- Per-item BAPI message: a RETURN entry with PARAMETER = 'POITEM' and ROW = item position. Otherwise the first E/A message of the PO, wrapped in M08. A commit failure appends TEXT-e02.
- Done items get icon_okay and M04, then are deleted from the grid. The summary is M02 with the count of done items. `&1` texts are filled with REPLACE and sent as `MESSAGE s001(00) WITH lv_text`.
- Status icons: icon_led_green = ready; icon_locked = not released (M03, skipped on action); icon_led_red = BAPI error.

# Decisions — ZMMR_HQ_HYB

## Phase 4 Wave 3 (sap-executor, Sonnet·medium)
- STATUS_0100 FORM sets the GUI status and title, then PERFORMs INIT_ALV_0100. The screen flow needs only `MODULE status_0100` in PBO, as the spec says. No separate init module.
- Added `EKKO-BSTYP = 'F'` to the SELECT. BAPI_PO_CHANGE handles purchase orders only, not RFQs or contracts. The spec is silent on this.
- S_EKORG is required in code only: E01 is raised on F8 (sy-ucomm = ONLI) when S_EKORG is empty. This keeps the multiple-selection popups usable. Reason: the authority check (c) runs per purchasing organization, so an empty EKORG would bypass it.
- Authority check: reads T024E for the EKORGs in the selection, then AUTHORITY-CHECK M_BEST_EKO ACTVT 02 for each. M07 is raised as an error on the first miss. UNCONFIRMED (c).
- UNCONFIRMED (a) in DELIVERY_COMPLETED_0100. UNCONFIRMED (b) in READ_DATA: LOEKZ = space on EKKO and EKPO; blocked items stay visible and BLK_REASON_ID is shown. UNCONFIRMED (c) in CHECK_COMMON_AUTHORITY.
- EKBE is read with the full key (zekkn, vgabe, gjahr, belnr, buzei), because FOR ALL ENTRIES drops duplicate rows and would give a wrong net GR.
- Per-item BAPI message: a RETURN entry with PARAMETER = 'POITEM' and ROW = item position. Otherwise the first E/A message of the PO, wrapped in M08. A commit failure appends TEXT-e02.
- Done items get icon_okay and M04, then are deleted from the grid. The summary is M02 with the count of done items. `&1` texts are filled with REPLACE and sent as `MESSAGE s001(00) WITH lv_text`.
- Status icons: icon_led_green = ready; icon_locked = not released (M03, skipped on action); icon_led_red = BAPI error.
- REFRESH re-runs START_OF_SELECTION and refreshes the grid. With SEL_MODE 'A', rows are read through get_selected_rows (row index = position in GT_ALV).
- No REPORT … MESSAGE-ID; messages use the explicit `(00)` form. No background-mode guard (the spec is silent).

# Result Artifact — show the completion report as a page (first creation only)

Companion of [`agent-pipeline.md`](agent-pipeline.md) § Phase 8. After the report is shown, the main thread publishes `report.html` as a private claude.ai Artifact and gives the user the link, so the result opens as a page instead of terminal text.

## When

All of these hold, else skip silently:

- **First creation** — this run created `{PROG}`: `state.json` had no completed `8_report` when the run started (a resumed first run counts). Never on a `--fix` run ([`cost-rules.md`](cost-rules.md) § 1c) or any later change round.
- **The host has the `Artifact` tool** (Claude Code with a claude.ai login). A host without it (sc4sap_web, plain API) skips — the web shows its own result page.
- Phase 8 finished and `report.md` exists (a `❌ BLOCKED` run never reaches Phase 8, so it never publishes).

## Steps (main thread)

1. Write `report.html` without asking: `node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/spec/md-to-html.mjs" .sc4sap/program/{PROG}/report.md` (`<PLUGIN_ROOT>` = two levels above this skill folder). The Phase 8 HTML line then offers `spec.html` only.
2. Read the whole `report.html` once — the Artifact rules require it before a publish of a file Claude did not write. This page is generated, not authored: publish it as-is, do not load `artifact-design` and do not edit it (its title is the report's H1; theme and layout come from `md-to-html.mjs`). A page problem is fixed in `md-to-html.mjs`, never by hand.
3. Publish: `Artifact({ file_path: "<abs path of report.html>", icon: "code", description: "{PROG} — create-program result, <YYYY-MM-DD>, <SAP system ID>" })`. No `url` (always a new artifact), no `capabilities`, no `pin`.
4. Print one line in the user's language: the link, and that it is private — only the user can open it until they share it from the page's Share menu.
5. Record the URL in `state.json` → `phases.8_report.artifact_url` and in `handoff.md`, so a later `--fix` run can name it. `--fix` runs never republish it.

## Content rules

- The page is the report as written — Evidence first, *Business questions decided automatically* (when `auto` decided any, [`../../common/review-questions.md`](../../common/review-questions.md) § 6), summary, *Decisions & Assumptions*. Nothing is added for the page.
- It carries system-specific names (programs, transport, system ID). The artifact is private by default; never share it or change its sharing for the user.
- A publish error is reported in one line and the run still ends normally — `report.md` / `report.html` on disk are the deliverable.
